name: seismic-historical-lineage-audit-v2
purpose: Permanent exact-byte provenance for historical seismic compression lineages considered for Master Portfolio V2. Memory, qualitative descriptions, or raw compression ratio alone are insufficient for promotion.

required: decoder-usable self-contained or fairly charged stream
strict hard-error verification under the declared epsilon contract
matched established comparator byte count on the identical numeric payload and epsilon semantics
promotion_rule.winner_rule: A lineage is portfolio-winner evidence only when it beats the strongest matched established comparator available in the audited experiment.

audits.decision: Do not promote yet. The surviving CI proves a real decodable byte stream, but does not report a matched SZ3/HPEZ comparator under the same present-day survey-global epsilon contract. Raw 10.818x compression is not itself a state-of-the-art win claim.

PR #28 is a Gorilla/XOR backend test, not the PULSE Stage A/B experiment. It expands incompressible random floats and is strong on constants; neither result is matched seismic portfolio-winner evidence.

Research-only. The analytic-subband stream narrowly beats matched SZ3 by about 1.4%, but is larger than the best official HPEZ orientation on the identical block and error contract. It therefore cannot be promoted as the strongest applicable recovered engine.

audits.principle: spatial+temporal spectral Top-N model plus decoder-visible quantized coefficients and sovereign 2*epsilon correction lattice

brady_pr56.scope: 128x8192 panel from PoroTomo/Brady DAS; epsilon from complete survey std
brady_pr56.note: Strong exact-byte matched-SZ3 evidence for the spectral principle on this Brady panel. PR #56 is an optimization pilot rather than the later fully materialized cross-survey container.

forge_pr100.container: self-contained; model and certificate decoded from bytes
forge_pr100.decision: Not a winner on FORGE. The exact self-contained transfer is larger than both matched SZ3 and the strongest matched HPEZ orientation.

soda_pr101.scope: three deterministic complete Soda Lake raw SEG-Y records at 10%, 50%, 90% object positions; per-shot 10%-std epsilon
soda_pr101.decision: Useful competitor but not the dominant Soda family. One of three shots loses to SZ3 and the two wins are only about 8-10%, whereas the recovered native Soda record/run engine has >2x historical and current global-epsilon evidence.

audits.decision: Keep Top-N as a protected distinct competitor because it is a genuine major Brady winner, but never universalize it into a replacement for native lattice engines. Eligibility and exact bytes must decide per scope.
